newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends weak on rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends weak on rate cut.

text.p: The Philippine peso closed down at 26.334 on Friday from 26.323 after the Central Bank cuts its overnight borrowing rate by 0.25 percentage point to ten percent, traders said.
That led banks to cover their short dollar positions in case T-bill rates move lower on Monday during the primary auction, they said.
The day's peso average was at 26.332 from 26.321.
Market volume rose to $295.10 million from $169.0 million.
The peso had fallen to a low of 26.34 in initial trades as a knee-jerk reaction to the rate cut. But it later gained due to dollar inflows.
"Overseas were selling dollars trying to catch the tail-end of this interest-rate differential," the dealer said.
Due to the hectic trading in the market, some traders said that the Central Bank intervened, while others said the Central Bank was a net buyer of dollars.
The peso will be dictated by the T-bill auction on Monday, traders said. -- LILIAN KARUNUNGAN (632) 841-8937
